title: Semiautomated longitudinal micro–computed tomography–based quantitative structural analysis of bone regeneration in osteoporotic rats
protocol: Put six week-old athymic ovariectomized rats on a 4 months low calcium diet consisting of 0.01% calcium and 0.77% phosphate.
Switch the rats back to normal diet after 4 months.
Induce anesthesia using 5% isoflurane in 100% oxygen.
Maintain anesthesia via nose cone at 2-3% isoflurane.
Apply toe pinch stimulus to ensure adequate plane of anesthesia.
Place the rat in dorsal recumbency on a heating pad set to 37°C.
Stretch the rat limbs using a magnetic fixator retraction system.
Shave the abdominal area.
Swab the shaved area with Betadine.
Swab the area with Chlorhexidine Gluconate 0.5%.
Swab the area with 70% ethanol.
Inject the rat with Carprofen (5 mg/kg BW, SQ).
Cut the skin using sterile surgical scissors.
Begin the incision 1 cm below the xiphoid process and extend it through the midline (~5-8 cm).
Make an incision of the aponeurosis through the linea alba to access the abdominal cavity.
Use retractors to expose the abdominal cavity.
Deflect the intestines to the rat’s right to expose the abdominal aorta and the left kidney.
Palpate the lumbar spine before proceeding.
Use thermocautery to expose the anterior aspect of lumbar vertebral bodies and isolate them from surrounding connective tissue and muscles.
Remove blood and residual tissue from the vertebrae using a cotton swab saturated with 3% hydrogen peroxide.
Drill a 5mm deep bone defect in the center of the vertebral body with a sterile drill bit (~2 mm in diameter).
Apply minimal pressure to ensure drilling through only the ventral cortex and underlying trabecular bone, avoiding the dorsal cortex.
Clean the defect using a cotton swab and apply pressure to stop bleeding if present.
Repeat step 13 on an adjacent vertebra to create a total of 2 defects per rat.
Return the intestines to the abdominal cavity.
Suture the aponeurosis in a continuous pattern with a vicryl synthetic absorbable surgical suture (3-0 Vicryl undyed 27" SH taper).
Close the skin using a monofilament nylon non-absorbable suture (4-0 Ethilon black 18" PC-3 conventional cutting) in a simple interrupted pattern.
Apply 100 μl of Dermabond on top of the skin sutures and between them to ensure complete closure of the skin.
Inject the rat with warm lactated Ringer’s solution (37°C) at a dose of 1CC/100g BW, SQ to prevent hypothermia and dehydration.
Inject the rat with Buprenorphine (0.5 mg/kg, SQ) for post-op pain relief.
Return the recovered animal on the heating pad to its cage after ensuring it is housed individually in a separate cage to prevent rat-to-rat mutilation of sutures and wounds.
Place chow soaked in water in a petri dish on the cage floor for a few days post-op to help rats reach the food.
Administer Carprofen (5 mg/kg BW, SQ) 24 hours post-surgery for pain relief.
Remove skin sutures while the animal is under 2% isoflurane anesthesia 10-14 days post-op.
Place the osteoporotic rat in an induction chamber of an anesthesia machine with a central scavenging system.
Induce anesthesia using 5% isoflurane in 100% oxygen and maintain via nose cone at 2-3% isoflurane.
Scan the rat using an in-vivo microCT scanner.
Repeat scanning for longitudinal analysis of bone regeneration.
Ensure all animals are scanned using the same settings (X-ray energy, scanning medium, intensity, voxel size, and image resolution) and in a similar orientation.
Contour the vertebra of interest.
Include all parts of the vertebra while excluding adjacent vertebrae parts.
Save the contoured vertebra as a separate file.
Measure the angle of the margins using a xy slice from the center of the defect for reference vertebra.
Use the measured angle to rotate the vertebra around the z-axis.
Measure the angle of the margins using a yz slice from the center of the defect for reference vertebra.
Use the measured angle to rotate the vertebra around the x-axis.
Flip the rotated vertebra by changing the xy plane to the zx plane.
Draw a circular contour of the defect using a slice from the center of the defect.
Copy and paste the circular contour on all slices in the defect.
Load DICOM files of both target and reference vertebrae into the main window of "Analyze" software.
Define the same output data type as the original DICOM files in the load menu.
Launch the “3-D Voxel Registration” module.
Input the reference vertebra as the “Base Volume” and the target vertebra as the “Match Volume”.
Click “Register” to register the vertebrae.
Save the registered file using the same data type.
Import the saved file into your microCT environment.
Apply the VOI defined for the reference vertebra to the registered target vertebra.
Check that the VOI and defect are concentric.
Send the VOI for evaluation using your microCT evaluation program.
Use the same parameters when analyzing all VOIs.
Set the threshold high enough to omit background noise with minimal loss of bone.
